verdict: DISCARD - overturned. Meta value was an estimator-coupling artifact, not length-prior signal.
recipe: 54 member probs + 4 length-bin one-hot + 18 shrinkage log-prior-ratio features (LO-prompt tables for train rows), cross-fitted LR class_weight=balanced, SGKF5 seed 42

decoupled_table_test.protocol: val tables from half A of the fold, stacker fit only on half B with LO-within-B tables

mechanism: The LO-table r-block for fit rows and the full-fold r-table for validation rows derive from the same fold's overlapping row set (~99.7% shared rows). In that coupled regime LR(C>=16) fits per-bin offsets that its own fold's validation rows reproduce (+0.10 BA, all folds). Under fully decoupled tables the effect INVERTS (-0.29). Real vs permuted bins are statistically indistinguishable in every arm (A4/m-sweep/decoupled), analytic post-hoc reweighting adds nothing, and per-row random scale-match blocks add nothing. Conclusion: zero deployable length-prior signal.
